Ambassador: An appointed representative of the Australian Medical Association (Victoria) Limited or ASMOF.
Association: The Australian Medical Association (Victoria) Limited (AMA) or the Australian Salaried Medical Officers Federation (Victoria Branch) (ASMOF).
Doctor: A registered medical practitioner employed by a Health Service as a Hospital Medical Officer, Medical Officer, Senior Medical Officer, Registrar, or a person enrolled in a General Practice Training Program.
Duty Hours: Those hours for which a Doctor is rostered or paid by the Hospital.
FFPPOA: First full pay period on or after.
HMO: Hospital Medical Officer — a Doctor with three or less years of experience who is not performing the duties of a Medical Officer or Registrar.
HSR: Health and safety representative (including a deputy health and safety representative).
MO: Medical Officer — a Doctor with three or more completed years of experience who is not performing the duties of a Registrar.
Parent Hospital: The Hospital that employs a Doctor (typically on a one-year contract) and which may direct the Doctor to work at a Rotation Hospital as part of a structured training program or to meet service demands.
Registrar: A Doctor appointed to an accredited Specialist training position, or who holds a position designated as such by the Health Service.
Rotation: A period during which a Doctor is directed to work at a Hospital other than the one by which they are employed, as part of a structured training program or to meet service demands.
Rotation Hospital: A hospital that receives a Doctor on rotation.
Shiftworker: For NES purposes, any Doctor required to work in excess of ordinary hours, or who works ordinary hours on more than 10 weekends (Saturday or Sunday or both) during the leave accrual year.
SMO: Senior Medical Officer — a Doctor employed as a Head of Department or equivalent role within the Health Service.
Specialist Medical College: A medical college accredited by the Australian Medical Council.
Statutory Body: The Department of Health (Victoria), formerly the Department of Health and Human Services (Victoria).
Stillborn Child: A child who weighs at least 400 grams at delivery or whose period of gestation was at least 20 weeks, who has not breathed since delivery, and whose heart has not beaten since delivery.
Training Time: A rostered period of 5 hours per week available to Registrars for training, free from service calls (except genuine medical emergencies or disaster situations).
VHIA: Victorian Hospitals' Industrial Association — the employers' representative body.
Week: Seven consecutive days reckoned from and to midnight on Saturday night.
WIRC Act: Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013 (Vic), or where applicable the Accident Compensation Act 1985 (Vic) or the Workers Compensation Act 1958 (Vic).
